locator: Overview, p. iii; Executive Summary pp. ES-3–ES-4.
context: PACE Center for Girls randomized follow-up; short-term outcomes and May 2017-dollar cost estimate remain distinct.
name: PACE randomly assigned 1,125 eligible Florida applicants across 14 centers.
description: The 2013–2015 evaluation assigned 673 girls to an offer of PACE and 452 to referrals for alternative community services. It evaluates a voluntary, nonresidential, year-round academic and social-service package.

context: PACE Center for Girls randomized follow-up; short-term outcomes and May 2017-dollar cost estimate remain distinct.
name: PACE’s net societal service cost was about $10,400 per program-group girl (May 2017 dollars).
description: The 12-month cost difference compares PACE and other services with control services. It adjusts PACE to a 7.9-month average stay, excludes participant opportunity costs, and is not a benefit-cost ratio.

values.value: May 2017 USD net societal service cost per program-group girl over the 12-month cost-analysis window.

locator: Table ES.1, p. ES-8; Table 3.1, p. 33.
context: PACE Center for Girls randomized follow-up; short-term outcomes and May 2017-dollar cost estimate remain distinct.
name: PACE increased days present in school by 9.8 in the first follow-up year (119.6 versus 109.8).
description: This regression-adjusted Florida public-school administrative-record result covers the calendar year after study enrollment. It is an attendance outcome, not a graduation effect.

values.value: Difference in number of school days present over the first follow-up calendar year, PACE minus control.

locator: Table ES.1, p. ES-8; Table 3.1, p. 33.
context: PACE Center for Girls randomized follow-up; short-term outcomes and May 2017-dollar cost estimate remain distinct.
name: PACE increased the high-school on-track composite by 13.4 percentage points (27.6% versus 14.2%).
description: The composite requires absence below 10% of enrolled days, no expulsion or suspension, and no core-course failure. It applies only to high-school students and is not observed graduation.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in high-school on-track composite during first follow-up year, PACE minus control.

context: PACE Center for Girls randomized follow-up; short-term outcomes and May 2017-dollar cost estimate remain distinct.
name: PACE increased credits earned as a share of credits attempted by 10.6 percentage points (77.5% versus 66.9%).
description: This regression-adjusted academic-year measure applies only to high-school students in Florida public-school records. The report found no statistically significant difference in total credits earned.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in academic-year credits earned as a share of credits attempted, PACE minus control.

context: PACE Center for Girls randomized follow-up; short-term outcomes and May 2017-dollar cost estimate remain distinct.
name: PACE reduced ever-suspended status by 16.7 percentage points in the first follow-up year (29.6% versus 46.4%).
description: This Florida public-school administrative-record measure covers the calendar year after study enrollment. It is a short-term disciplinary outcome, not a later justice-system effect.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in ever being suspended during first follow-up calendar year, PACE minus control.

locator: Table ES.1, p. ES-8; juvenile-justice discussion pp. ES-9–ES-10.
context: PACE Center for Girls randomized follow-up; short-term outcomes and May 2017-dollar cost estimate remain distinct.
name: PACE showed no statistically significant 18-month difference in girls incurring a juvenile-justice charge (+0.8 points; 22.0% versus 21.2%).
description: The full-sample Florida juvenile-justice administrative-record difference was not statistically significant. A charge is the report’s juvenile-justice term and should not be relabeled as an adult arrest.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in incurring one or more juvenile-justice charges during 18 months after random assignment, PACE minus control.
